```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
library(lazer)
```

lazer gathers the readers and writers of day-to-day work. They share three
habits: they are quiet when all is well, they report every problem in one
message, and they never drop or reinterpret data without saying so.

## Many files at once: `read_files()`

A production script often starts with one `read_*()` call per file.
`read_files()` replaces the block: it expands paths with glue syntax,
checks that every file exists before reading anything, picks the reader
from the extension, and names the results.

```{r}
lst <- read_files("data/dat{2020:2023}.parquet", names = 2020:2023)

df <- read_files("data/dat{2020:2023}.parquet", names = 2020:2023,
                 out = "bind", .id = "year")
```

A file that fails to read does not stop the others; all failures are
reported together at the end. When the files cannot be stacked as they
are, only the columns whose types clash are re-typed, and the warning names
them. CSV files are read as semicolon-separated with a decimal comma.

## Excel: `read_workbook()` and `inspect_excel()`

`readxl` reads the smallest rectangle around every non-empty cell, so a
title becomes the header and a source note becomes a row. `read_workbook()`
reads every sheet and finds the table on each instead, and one warning lists
what was left outside:

```{r}
sheets <- read_workbook("data/report.xlsx")
```

Choose the area yourself when needed: a range, one per sheet, a named range
from the workbook, or a defined Excel table.

```{r}
df     <- read_workbook("data/report.xlsx", range = "Report!B3:F40")
sheets <- read_workbook("data/report.xlsx", range = c(Report = "B3:F40", Notes = NA))
sales  <- read_workbook("data/report.xlsx", range = "Salesdata")
tables <- read_workbook("data/report.xlsx", table = TRUE)
```

`inspect_excel()` runs the same check without reading, and returns the
blocks outside the table as a tibble, empty when the layout is clean.

## Presentable Excel output: `write_excel()`

```{r}
write_excel(list(Overview = overview, Detail = detail), "out.xlsx")
write_excel(list(Appendix = extra), "out.xlsx", mode = "append")
```

Headers are bold and frozen, and large numbers get a thousand separator
without rounding the stored values. Year-like columns are left alone.

## Greenlandic TA files

`read_ta()` reads both layouts and recognises which by itself.
`write_ta()` writes the one you name, since it has to match the receiver,
and refuses any value it cannot write exactly, listing every one.
`convert_ta()` converts a file between the layouts.

```{r}
ta <- read_ta("ta.file")
write_ta(ta, "out.ta", version = 2)
convert_ta("old.ta", "new.ta", to = 2)
```

Both layouts are written as one small table each at the top of
`R/ta.R`. The reader and the writer only follow those tables, so a change in
a layout is a change there.
